trial_court: Family Court, Raigarh, Civil Suit No. 194/2025
case_name: Akash Ahirwar vs Smt. Ragini Dadoriya Ahirwar
facts_of_case: Marriage between parties was solemnized on 20.02.2023 and out of the wedlock a child was born on 22.02.2024. Matrimonial discord arose leading to proceedings under Section 13(A) of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 seeking dissolution of marriage. Respondent-wife moved application under Section 24 for maintenance pendente lite and litigation expenses.

legal_principles.principle: The objective of granting interim/permanent alimony is to ensure that the dependent spouse is not reduced to destitution or vagrancy on account of the failure of the marriage, and not as a punishment to the other spouse.
legal_principles.held: There is no straitjacket formula for fixing the quantum of maintenance to be awarded.

legal_principles.principle: The court must take into consideration the status of the parties and the capacity of the spouse to pay for her or his support.
legal_principles.held: An order of interim maintenance is conditional on the circumstance that the wife or husband who makes a claim has no independent income, sufficient for her or his support.

legal_principles.principle: A careful and just balance must be drawn between all relevant factors.
legal_principles.held: The test for determination of maintenance in matrimonial disputes depends on the financial status of the respondent.

outcome.final_order: Impugned order set aside; maintenance pendente lite to be re-determined by trial court.
